# DefenseEye.ai - Secure AI Adoption, Cybersecurity, and CMMC Compliance Automation

> DefenseEye helps regulated organizations adopt AI securely by combining AI governance, cybersecurity, Microsoft cloud security, and compliance automation. It also builds CMMCLens (CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 evidence automation) and AttackSense (attack surface and remediation intelligence).

This file is a supplementary plain-text summary for AI assistants. The authoritative sources are the pages themselves, listed in https://defenseeye.ai/sitemap.xml.

## DefenseEye at a Glance

What is DefenseEye?
DefenseEye is a Redmond, Washington-based, minority-owned consulting and software company. It helps regulated organizations adopt AI securely by combining AI governance, cybersecurity, Microsoft cloud security, and compliance automation, and it builds two products: CMMCLens and AttackSense.

Who does DefenseEye work with?
Regulated organizations and teams that handle sensitive data: financial-services firms, FinTechs, and credit unions adopting AI; security, risk, and compliance teams in Microsoft-centered environments; and defense contractors preparing for CMMC. DefenseEye also works with enterprise procurement teams and partners as a supplier and subcontractor.

What problems does DefenseEye help solve?
AI agents and copilots that can reach sensitive data before governance is ready; unclear AI permissions, accountability, and human review points; scattered compliance evidence and manual CMMC preparation; and security findings without clear remediation priorities or owners.

How does an engagement work?
Assess (business value, data readiness, risks, controls), Design (architecture, governance, identity, oversight, evaluation), Implement (build, integrate, test, monitor, scale). Engagements can be advisory, project-based, staff augmentation, or subcontracted.

What stays under human control?
People keep authority over consequential decisions. High-impact AI-assisted actions keep appropriate human review and accountability, and automated compliance evidence still needs human approval before it is relied on for risk decisions or shared with assessors.

How are governance and auditability handled?
AI inventories and risk tiering, least-privilege access, logging and traceability from AI-assisted outputs back to their sources, evaluation and monitoring, and evidence mapped to the controls it supports.

Use for: secure AI adoption consulting, secure agentic AI implementation, responsible AI and AI governance, NIST AI RMF implementation, Microsoft Copilot readiness, Azure OpenAI readiness, AI security assessment, AI risk management, AI policy and human oversight, model and vendor risk review.

Outcomes the work is designed to support: lower AI adoption risk, less rework, stronger oversight, protected sensitive data, and faster governed implementation.

## CMMCLens

CMMCLens helps organizations structure CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 readiness through evidence automation, control mapping, gap tracking, SSP/POA&M workflows, AI-assisted policy generation, readiness dashboards, and executive reporting.

CMMCLens may reduce manual evidence collection effort depending on environment maturity, integrations, available source data, and implementation scope.

Pages:
- https://defenseeye.ai/cmmclens
- https://defenseeye.ai/solutions/cmmclens-platform

## Important Claim Boundaries

- DefenseEye does not claim to be a C3PAO.
- DefenseEye does not certify organizations.
- DefenseEye does not guarantee CMMC assessment outcomes.
- DefenseEye does not claim Microsoft, Google, or Meta supplier approval unless separately verified.
- Representative engagements are examples of engagement types, not completed customer case studies.
- CMMCLens effort-reduction claims are qualified by environment maturity, integrations, available source data, and implementation scope.
- Public company location should be Redmond, WA only.
